name: WordPress MCP Adapter
short_description: Connect to WordPress 6.9+ and expose its Abilities API (posts, pages, media, users) as MCP tools.
store_description: Bridges WordPress 6.9+ Abilities API with the Model Context Protocol via the official WordPress MCP Adapter plugin (v0.7.1+, available directly from WordPress.org plugin directory or GitHub). No Composer needed since v0.6.1 — the vendor/ folder is bundled. Authentication uses WordPress core Application Passwords via HTTP Basic Auth. The default server exposes three meta-tools: mcp-adapter/discover-abilities (lists public abilities), mcp-adapter/get-ability-info (returns schema), and mcp-adapter/execute-ability (runs the ability). Any plugin or theme ability marked with meta.mcp.public = true becomes automatically discoverable. HTTPS is required on production sites — Application Passwords are disabled over plain HTTP.
description: Connect to a WordPress site running the official MCP Adapter plugin (Abilities API).

WORDPRESS_URL.title: WordPress Site URL
WORDPRESS_URL.description: Base URL of your WordPress site without trailing slash. Example: https://mysite.com. HTTPS is required on production.

WORDPRESS_USERNAME.title: WordPress Username
WORDPRESS_USERNAME.description: Your WordPress account username. Use a dedicated account with limited permissions, not the admin account.

WORDPRESS_APP_PASSWORD.title: Application Password
WORDPRESS_APP_PASSWORD.description: Generate in WP Admin → Users → Profile → Application Passwords. The spaces in the generated password are OK — WordPress accepts them verbatim.

usage_hint: This MCP server exposes three meta-tools, not direct capabilities. WORKFLOW: (1) ALWAYS start by calling 'mcp-adapter/discover-abilities' with no arguments to list what WordPress plugins/themes have exposed. (2) For each ability you want to use, call 'mcp-adapter/get-ability-info' with {ability_name} to get its input schema. (3) Finally call 'mcp-adapter/execute-ability' with {ability_name, parameters} to run it. Never skip step 1 — abilities are installed dynamically and guessing their names will fail. If discover-abilities returns an empty list, the user has not registered any abilities yet (plugins must call wp_register_ability with meta.mcp.public=true).
